title: The Sunday Read: ‘What Does Sustainable Living Look Like? Maybe Like Uruguay’

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是Benjamin Poulin，我是Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店当DJ的那个黑胶唱片时代，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后把DJ台变成一个活生生的、快闪式的博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、已有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: For most of human history, it seemed as if there was only one way to get people out of poverty or to improve one's quality of life, and that was burn more oil.
sentences.zh: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，似乎只有一种方法能让人们摆脱贫困或提高生活质量，那就是燃烧更多的石油。

sentences.en: Whether you were driving a new car or buying a bigger house or starting a new industry, that was the end result you were resigned to.
sentences.zh: 无论你是开上新车、买了大房子，还是开创了新产业，这都是你不得不接受的最终结果。

sentences.en: But climate change has put an end to that,
sentences.zh: 但气候变化已经终结了这一切，

sentences.en: because there's simply no way for all the developing economies around the world to increase consumption while also meeting global emissions goals.
sentences.zh: 因为全球的发展中经济体根本无法在增加消费的同时，又达到全球排放目标。

sentences.en: Consumption on that level is just not sustainable.
sentences.zh: 那种水平的消费是不可持续的。

sentences.en: A lot of long-range outlooks on climate change have vividly rendered what a world like that would look like if we exceeded our emissions goals, and it's terrifying.
sentences.zh: 许多关于气候变化的长期展望都生动地描绘了如果我们超过排放目标，世界会变成什么样，那景象令人恐惧。

sentences.en: Still, as a climate reporter, and also just as a human, I found a better future than that pretty hard to picture.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，作为一名气候记者，同时也是一个普通人，我发现要想象出一个比那更好的未来相当困难。

sentences.en: Were there even places around the world where we could get a glimpse of what sustainable living would actually look like?
sentences.zh: 世界上是否真的存在一些地方，能让我们一窥可持续生活到底是什么样子的？

sentences.en: And as it turns out, yeah, there are.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，确实有。

sentences.en: My name's Noah Gallagher-Shannon, and I'm a contributor to the New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫Noah Gallagher-Shannon，是《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: This week's Sunday Read is about my search for a model of sustainable development.
sentences.zh: 本周的《周日阅读》讲述了我寻找可持续发展模式的过程。

sentences.en: And it's also about what we as consumers and global citizens might be able to learn from that model.
sentences.zh: 同时也探讨了我们作为消费者和全球公民，能从这种模式中学到什么。

sentences.en: So when you think about countries committed to climate action, you probably first think about, for example, Denmark or Iceland.
sentences.zh: 当你想到那些致力于气候行动的国家时，你可能首先会想到丹麦或冰岛。

sentences.en: But there's one that might surprise you.
sentences.zh: 但有一个国家可能会让你感到惊讶。

sentences.en: It's a South American country of just three and a half million people that's leading an incredible green revolution.
sentences.zh: 那是一个南美国家，人口仅有350万，却正在引领一场令人难以置信的绿色革命。

sentences.en: One of the smallest and least densely populated countries on Earth.
sentences.zh: 它是地球上人口最稀少、面积最小的国家之一。

sentences.en: Tucked away between Brazil and Argentina, its capital is full of these old Art Deco apartment buildings and cobblestone streets.
sentences.zh: 它坐落在巴西和阿根廷之间，首都到处都是装饰艺术风格的旧公寓楼和鹅卵石街道。

sentences.en: And there's this wonderful walkway along the river, La Rambla.
sentences.zh: 河边还有一条美妙的步道，叫La Rambla。

sentences.en: The rest of the country is this vast expanse of grasslands and rolling hills.
sentences.zh: 这个国家的其他地方是一望无际的草原和连绵起伏的丘陵。

sentences.en: It's reminiscent of what Americans might picture when they think of Kansas or Nebraska.
sentences.zh: 这让人想起美国人想到堪萨斯州或内布拉斯加州时的景象。

sentences.en: In this country, where cattle outnumber people four to one, it's Uruguay.
sentences.zh: 在这个牛的数量是人口四倍的国家，它就是乌拉圭。

sentences.en: Uruguay is really a Goldilocks of countries.
sentences.zh: 乌拉圭确实是一个“金发姑娘”式的国家（指各方面条件恰到好处）。

sentences.en: Its carbon footprint is small enough that it's within range of the two or so tons of carbon emissions per person
sentences.zh: 它的碳足迹足够小，大约在人均两吨左右，

sentences.en: that we need to have if we're going to keep global warming around 1.5 degrees Celsius.
sentences.zh: 这是我们要将全球变暖控制在1.5摄氏度以内所必须达到的水平。

sentences.en: But it also has a standard of living high enough that I think a lot of people could aspire to it, or they'd feel comfortable living that way.
sentences.zh: 但它的生活水平又足够高，我认为很多人都会向往，或者会觉得那样生活很舒适。

sentences.en: Uruguay's history plays a big part in this story.
sentences.zh: 乌拉圭的历史在这个故事中扮演了重要角色。

sentences.en: From the early 70s to the mid-80s, Uruguay was under a dictatorship.
sentences.zh: 从70年代初到80年代中期，乌拉圭处于独裁统治之下。

sentences.en: The economy collapsed, hundreds of thousands of people were exiled, and an estimated 1 in 500 people were in prison.
sentences.zh: 经济崩溃，数十万人流亡，估计每500人中就有一人入狱。

sentences.en: When the country emerged, there was a real focus on how to best ensure a stable future.
sentences.zh: 当这个国家走出阴霾时，人们真正关注的是如何最好地确保一个稳定的未来。

sentences.en: But Uruguay also had an energy problem.
sentences.zh: 但乌拉圭当时也面临能源问题。

sentences.en: Its economy was yoked to global oil commodity prices.
sentences.zh: 其经济被全球石油大宗商品价格所束缚。

sentences.en: And they were scrambling to meet rising demand.
sentences.zh: 他们正忙于应对不断增长的需求。

sentences.en: They suffered rolling blackouts and oil shortages throughout the country.
sentences.zh: 全国各地饱受轮流停电和石油短缺之苦。

sentences.en: But then instead of merely trying to solve an oil shortage, they thought about how to diversify their power sources to renewables like solar and wind.
sentences.zh: 但后来，他们没有仅仅试图解决石油短缺问题，而是思考如何将能源来源多样化，转向太阳能和风能等可再生能源。

sentences.en: And then an even more interesting thing happened.
sentences.zh: 然后发生了一件更有趣的事情。

sentences.en: Once the country changed to a green grid, people began to change their own behavior too, little by little.
sentences.zh: 一旦国家转向绿色电网，人们的行为也开始一点一点地发生改变。

sentences.en: They put solar-powered hot water heaters on top of their houses.
sentences.zh: 他们在屋顶上安装了太阳能热水器。

sentences.en: They used timers so that they would only use electricity at night when it was cheaper.
sentences.zh: 他们使用定时器，只在电价更便宜的夜间使用电力。

sentences.en: They shopped secondhand.
sentences.zh: 他们购买二手商品。

sentences.en: And they resisted buying that new car, that new couch, just because they could afford it.
sentences.zh: 他们抵制购买新车、新沙发，即使他们买得起。

sentences.en: In Uruguay, no single industry or culture is as dominant as cattle ranching.
sentences.zh: 在乌拉圭，没有任何单一产业或文化能像养牛业那样占据主导地位。

sentences.en: But beef is also one of the most carbon-intensive products in our diet.
sentences.zh: 但牛肉也是我们饮食中碳排放最密集的食物之一。

sentences.en: And so they've begun imagining ways of making even this industry more sustainable.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们开始设想让这个行业也变得更可持续的方法。

sentences.en: It was almost as if this transition to green energy had flipped a big switch.
sentences.zh: 就好像这种向绿色能源的转型按下了某个巨大的开关。

sentences.en: It wasn't a movement that had spurred a policy, but a policy that had spurred a movement.
sentences.zh: 这不是一场推动了政策的运动，而是一项政策推动了一场运动。

sentences.en: Even if Uruguayans didn't see themselves as environmentalists, they were beginning to see themselves as something else, climate actors.
sentences.zh: 即使乌拉圭人并不认为自己是环保主义者，他们也开始以另一种身份看待自己：气候行动者。

sentences.en: So often in the conversation about climate change, this dilemma comes up.
sentences.zh: 在关于气候变化的讨论中，经常会出现这样一个困境。

sentences.en: Is it the consumer's responsibility to change their behavior?
sentences.zh: 改变行为是消费者的责任吗？

sentences.en: Or rather, should it be corporations and governments that should change their practices?
sentences.zh: 还是说，应该由企业和政府来改变他们的做法？

sentences.en: You could say that this story comes out of my dissatisfaction with the premise of those questions.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，这个故事源于我对这些问题前提的不满。

sentences.en: Why are they at odds with each other?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们是对立的呢？

sentences.en: Isn't it possible for all of them to change together?
sentences.zh: 难道它们不能一起改变吗？

sentences.en: So here's my article.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的文章。

sentences.en: What Does Sustainable Living Look Like?
sentences.zh: 可持续生活是什么样的？

sentences.en: Maybe Like Uruguay.
sentences.zh: 也许就像乌拉圭那样。

sentences.en: Read by James Patrick Cronin.
sentences.zh: 由James Patrick Cronin朗读。

sentences.en: This was recorded by Autumn.
sentences.zh: 由Autumn录制。

sentences.en: To listen to more stories from The New York Times, The New Yorker, Vanity Fair, The Atlantic,
sentences.zh: 想在智能手机上收听更多来自《纽约时报》、《纽约客》、《名利场》、《大西洋月刊》

sentences.en: and other publications on your smartphone, download Autumn on the App Store or the Play Store.
sentences.zh: 以及其他出版物的故事，请在App Store或Play Store下载Autumn。

sentences.en: Visit Autumn.
sentences.zh: 访问Autumn。

sentences.en: That's A-U-D-M dot com for more details.
sentences.zh: 网址是A-U-D-M点com，了解更多详情。

sentences.en: Let's say you live in the typical American household.
sentences.zh: 假设你住在一个典型的美国家庭里。

sentences.en: It doesn't exist, not in any sense except in a data set, but it's easy enough to imagine.
sentences.zh: 它并不存在，除了在数据集里，但在现实中并不存在，不过这很容易想象。

sentences.en: Maybe it's your aunts or your neighbors or a bit like your own.
sentences.zh: 也许是你的阿姨、邻居，或者有点像你自己的家。

sentences.en: Since more than half of us live outside big cities, it's probably in a middle-class suburb like Fox Lake, north of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 由于我们中超过一半的人住在城市之外，它可能位于芝加哥北部福克斯湖（Fox Lake）这样的中产阶级郊区。

sentences.en: You picked it because it's affordable and not a terrible commute to your job.
sentences.zh: 你选择这里是因为它负担得起，而且去上班的通勤路程也不算太糟糕。

sentences.en: Your house is about 2,200 square feet, a split-level ranch, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 你的房子大约2200平方英尺（约204平方米），可能是一栋错层式牧场住宅。

sentences.en: You're in your mid-30s and just welcomed your first child.
sentences.zh: 你三十多岁，刚刚迎来了第一个孩子。

sentences.en: Together with your partner, you make about $70,000 a year, some of which goes toward the 11,000 kilowatts of electricity
sentences.zh: 你和伴侣每年的收入约为7万美元，其中一部分用于支付11000千瓦的电力，

sentences.en: and 37,000 cubic feet of natural gas you use to heat the house, play video games, and dry your clothes.
sentences.zh: 以及37000立方英尺的天然气，用来给房子供暖、玩电子游戏和烘干衣服。

sentences.en: You take six or seven plane flights a year to visit your mom after her surgery or attend a conference and drive about 25,000 miles,
sentences.zh: 你每年坐六七次飞机，去探望手术后的母亲或参加会议，开车行驶约25000英里，

sentences.en: most of which you barely register anymore as you listen to Joe Rogan or Bad Bunny.
sentences.zh: 当你听着Joe Rogan或Bad Bunny的节目时，大部分路程你甚至已经没什么感觉了。

sentences.en: Maybe twice a month, you stop at Target and pick up six or seven things.
sentences.zh: 也许一个月两次，你会去塔吉特（Target）百货买六七样东西。

sentences.en: Double-sided tape, an extra toothbrush, an inflatable mattress.
sentences.zh: 双面胶、多余的牙刷、充气床垫。

sentences.en: You believe that the power and goods you consume are changing the climate, but do not believe in your ability to stop it.
sentences.zh: 你相信你消耗的能源和商品正在改变气候，但不相信自己有能力阻止它。

sentences.en: So, when you come into more money, no matter your political leanings or education, you buy a bigger house, another car, more stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你有了更多的钱，无论你的政治倾向或受教育程度如何，你都会买更大的房子、更多的车、更多的东西。

sentences.en: You barely notice, but in the years since 1988, when James Hansen testified that our burning of fossil fuels was destroying the conditions for life,
sentences.zh: 你几乎没有注意到，但自1988年James Hansen作证说我们燃烧化石燃料正在破坏生命生存条件以来的这些年里，

sentences.en: your home has grown by about 1,000 square feet, and you've bought another car, an SUV that's itself 25% larger, even though you have fewer kids.
sentences.zh: 你的家已经扩大了约1000平方英尺，你还买了一辆车，一辆本身就大25%的SUV，尽管你的孩子变少了。

sentences.en: All these choices compound so quietly that if you're lucky enough to earn over $100,000 a year, you wind up helping your relatively small social group, about a fifth of Americans,
sentences.zh: 所有这些选择都在悄无声息地累积，如果你足够幸运，年收入超过10万美元，你最终会帮助你所在的相对较小的社会群体（约占美国人的五分之一），

sentences.en: contribute around a third of household emissions.
sentences.zh: 贡献了约三分之一的家庭排放量。

sentences.en: Even if you don't, by the end of the year, your carbon bill is world-historically anomalous, but normal among your neighbors.
sentences.zh: 即使你没有达到这个收入，到年底，你的碳账单在世界历史上也是异常的，但在你的邻居中却是正常的。

sentences.en: 17 tons for transportation,
sentences.zh: 交通运输17吨，

sentences.en: 14 tons for housing,
sentences.zh: 住房14吨，

sentences.en: 8 tons for food,
sentences.zh: 食品8吨，

sentences.en: 6 tons for services,
sentences.zh: 服务6吨，

sentences.en: 5 tons for goods.
sentences.zh: 商品5吨。

sentences.en: That household total, 50 tons, represents a carbon footprint of about 25 tons per person.
sentences.zh: 家庭总排放量为50吨，相当于人均约25吨的碳足迹。

sentences.en: It's a figure that eclipses the global median by a factor of 5 and is nowhere close to where it needs to be if you, we, want to stave off the worst of warming's effects,
sentences.zh: 这个数字是全球中位数的5倍，而且如果你、我们想要避免气候变暖带来的最严重影响，它离目标还差得远，

sentences.en: around 2 tons per person.
sentences.zh: 目标是人均约2吨。

sentences.en: The task of shrinking our societal footprint is the most urgent problem of our era, and perhaps the most intractable.
sentences.zh: 缩小我们社会足迹的任务是我们这个时代最紧迫的问题，也可能是最棘手的问题。

sentences.en: For most experts, the first steps are obvious and yield the largest and least invasive cuts.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数专家来说，第一步是显而易见的，而且能带来最大且干扰最小的减排效果。

sentences.en: Since electricity makes up about 25% of the United States' 5 billion or so tons of yearly emissions, it more than likely begins with decarbonizing the grid.
sentences.zh: 由于电力约占美国每年约50亿吨排放量的25%，这很可能从电网脱碳开始。

sentences.en: Next comes a push to electrify the transportation sector and regulate industrial production.
sentences.zh: 接下来是推动交通部门电气化和规范工业生产。

sentences.en: Each contributes about 27 and 24% of emissions, respectively.
sentences.zh: 它们分别贡献了约27%和24%的排放量。

sentences.en: Then come several smaller cuts to the buildings we live in and the appliances we use, from policies already having success in Europe and Canada,
sentences.zh: 然后是对我们居住的建筑和使用的电器进行一些较小的削减，这些政策在欧洲和加拿大已经取得了成功，

sentences.en: replacing gas-burning furnaces with electric heat pumps, updating building efficiencies, and banning air conditioners and fridges that use hydrofluorocarbon.
sentences.zh: 包括用电动热泵取代燃气炉、提高建筑能效，以及禁止使用氢氟碳化物的空调和冰箱。

sentences.en: Exactly how much all these cuts reduce our footprints is difficult to say because our country spans an entire continent with several climates.
sentences.zh: 所有这些削减到底能减少多少足迹很难说，因为我们的国家横跨整个大陆，气候多样。

sentences.en: But modeling by energy innovation suggests that even after enacting dozens of subsidies, new efficiency standards, and introducing new technologies, by 2050,
sentences.zh: 但能源创新机构的模型显示，即使在实施了数十项补贴、新的能效标准并引入新技术之后，到2050年，

sentences.en: it might only reduce our emissions by half.
sentences.zh: 它可能也只能将我们的排放量减少一半。

sentences.en: This is the problem with any climate policy, big or small.
sentences.zh: 这就是任何气候政策（无论大小）所面临的问题。

sentences.en: It requires an imaginative leap.
sentences.zh: 它需要一次想象力的飞跃。

sentences.en: While the math of decarbonization and electric mobilization is clear, the future lifestyle it implies isn't always.
sentences.zh: 虽然脱碳和电力动员的数学计算很清晰，但它所暗示的未来生活方式却并非总是如此。

sentences.en: Right-wing commenters sometimes seize upon this fact to caricature any climate policy as a forced retreat from modernity,
sentences.zh: 右翼评论员有时会抓住这一事实，将任何气候政策讽刺为被迫从现代性中撤退，

sentences.en: Americans forced to live in ecopods, while on the left, any accounting seems to cloud the urgency of the moment.
sentences.zh: 美国人被迫住在生态舱里；而在左翼，任何核算似乎都会掩盖当下的紧迫性。

sentences.en: A majority of emissions come from just 100 or so corporations, activists argue, a concentration of industrial production that, once decarbonized, could slash the footprint
sentences.zh: 活动人士认为，大部分排放来自大约100家企业，这种工业生产的集中度一旦脱碳，就能削减每一盏壁灯和每一个三明治背后的足迹。

sentences.en: beneath every wall sconce and sandwich.
sentences.zh: （此处原文为“beneath every wall sconce and sandwich”，意指从微小生活细节到工业生产的全面覆盖）

sentences.en: Even if it were true, these arguments conveniently ignore one uncomfortable fact.
sentences.zh: 即使这是真的，这些论点也方便地忽略了一个令人不安的事实。

sentences.en: Walmart, ExxonMobil, and Berkshire Hathaway didn't burn that fuel on their own.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛、埃克森美孚和伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司并不是自己燃烧了这些燃料。

sentences.en: We paid them to, or burned it ourselves because the way we live depends on it.
sentences.zh: 是我们付钱让他们烧的，或者是因为我们的生活方式依赖于它，我们自己烧的。

sentences.en: By any standard,
sentences.zh: 无论从什么标准来看，

sentences.en: American lives have become excessive and indulgent, full of large homes, long trips, aisles of choices, and app-delivered convenience.
sentences.zh: 美国人的生活已经变得过度和放纵，充满了大房子、长途旅行、琳琅满目的选择和应用程序带来的便利。

sentences.en: If the possibilities of the future are already narrowing to the one being painted by science with increasing lucidity, it strains even the most vivid imagination
sentences.zh: 如果未来的可能性已经缩小到科学界日益清晰地描绘的那一种，那么如果不改变行为，

sentences.en: to picture it widening again without a change in behavior.
sentences.zh: 即使是最丰富的想象力也难以想象它会再次拓宽。

sentences.en: This isn't an American crisis alone.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是美国的危机。

sentences.en: It was a view I found shared in some of the richest neighborhoods as well.
sentences.zh: 我在一些最富裕的社区也发现了同样的观点。

sentences.en: In Positos, at a cafe along the river, an economist named Paula Cobas told me that many felt misled by the transition.
sentences.zh: 在波西托斯（Positos）河边的一家咖啡馆里，一位名叫保拉·科巴斯（Paula Cobas）的经济学家告诉我，许多人觉得被这次转型误导了。

sentences.en: It reduced the cost of generation, so people naturally expected it would reduce their household bills, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，这降低了发电成本，所以人们自然期望它能降低家庭账单。

sentences.en: But it never happened.
sentences.zh: 但这从未发生。

sentences.en: While some felt proud of the international recognition, others wondered if the transition had merely been politically convenient.
sentences.zh: 虽然有些人为这种国际认可感到自豪，但另一些人则怀疑这种转型是否仅仅是出于政治上的便利。

sentences.en: Cobas gave the example of transportation.
sentences.zh: 科巴斯以交通为例。

sentences.en: Though the government subsidized electric cars, few could afford them.
sentences.zh: 尽管政府补贴电动汽车，但很少有人买得起。

sentences.en: So, rather than rely on mass transit, which remained crowded and slow, people simply bought cheap cars.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们没有依赖依然拥挤且缓慢的公共交通，而是直接买了廉价汽车。

sentences.en: Cobas' misgivings about the reach of certain green policies, about their awkward collisions
sentences.zh: 科巴斯对某些绿色政策的覆盖范围及其与乌拉圭生活现实之间尴尬冲突的担忧，

sentences.en: with the realities of Uruguayan life, reminded me of something a man in the Ascentamiento said to me.
sentences.zh: 让我想起了定居点里的一位男士对我所说的话。

sentences.en: Nobody has confronted the real problem.
sentences.zh: 没有人面对真正的问题。

sentences.en: How will the country grow?
sentences.zh: 这个国家将如何发展？

sentences.en: In many ways, it was the question facing every community.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这正是每个社区都面临的问题。

sentences.en: I thought of a single dad I met in Montevideo, who said I shouldn't think of his country as a model or example.
sentences.zh: 我想起在蒙得维的亚遇到的一位单身父亲，他说我不应该把他的国家视为一种模式或榜样。

sentences.en: It was too small, its progress too troubled.
sentences.zh: 它太小了，它的进步也太坎坷了。

sentences.en: It was more like a laboratory for the rest of the world, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，它更像是世界其他地方的一个实验室。

sentences.en: We often picture the future as a kind of growth, a set of possibilities to expand and realize, but maybe it could also be the opposite, a present to reconcile and safeguard.
sentences.zh: 我们经常把未来想象成一种增长，一系列可以扩展和实现的可能，但也许它也可以是相反的，一个需要调和与守护的现在。

sentences.en: Part of the reason America has become so paralyzed by climate change is precisely that we've failed
sentences.zh: 美国之所以被气候变化搞得如此瘫痪，部分原因恰恰在于我们未能

sentences.en: to acknowledge the limits it imposes on where we can live, the things we can have, the household we can envision.
sentences.zh: 承认它对我们居住的地方、我们拥有的东西、我们所能设想的家庭生活所施加的限制。

sentences.en: This is a particularly difficult idea to sell to a country perched atop decades of accrued wealth, which was itself amassed by generations imagining further comfort and choice.
sentences.zh: 对于一个建立在数十年积累的财富之上的国家来说，这是一个特别难以接受的想法，而这些财富本身就是由几代人对更多舒适和选择的想象所积累起来的。

sentences.en: But if there was something dangerously naive about thinking America could aspire to be Uruguay,
sentences.zh: 但如果认为美国可以渴望成为乌拉圭是一种危险的幼稚，

sentences.en: there was also every reason to think it might one day become some version of it anyway.
sentences.zh: 那么也有充分的理由认为它迟早会变成某种形式的乌拉圭。

sentences.en: As the climate worsens, driving ever more natural disasters and resource scarcity, the economy
sentences.zh: 随着气候恶化，导致越来越多的自然灾害和资源匮乏，经济

sentences.en: will naturally become more constrained with it, pushing prices higher and choices lower.
sentences.zh: 也将随之变得更加受限，从而推高价格并减少选择。

sentences.en: If I couldn't fathom a reconciliatory politics inspired by a guerrilla, could I imagine fewer hamburgers, more expensive gas, the same apartment?
sentences.zh: 如果我无法想象一种受游击队启发的和解政治，我能想象少吃汉堡、汽油更贵、住同样的公寓吗？

sentences.en: By the time I boarded a plane home, lines of container ships lingered offshore.
sentences.zh: 当我登上回家的飞机时，一排排集装箱船仍停泊在近海。

sentences.en: In the coming months, gas prices spiked, inflation climbed, and the price of energy began to strangle
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几个月里，汽油价格飙升，通货膨胀加剧，能源价格开始扼杀

sentences.en: Europe.
sentences.zh: 欧洲。

sentences.en: No future seemed as certain as a less abundant one.
sentences.zh: 似乎没有哪个未来比一个资源不再那么丰富的未来更确定了。

sentences.en: On August 16th, several months after I returned home, President Biden signed the most significant
sentences.zh: 8月16日，在我回国几个月后，拜登总统签署了有史以来最重要的

sentences.en: climate legislation ever passed, the Inflation Reduction Act, which included a package aimed at lowering carbon emissions in the transportation and energy sectors.
sentences.zh: 气候立法——《通胀削减法案》，其中包括旨在降低交通和能源部门碳排放的一揽子计划。

sentences.en: Independent modeling by Rhodium Group, a research firm in New York, estimated that the bill would cut emissions by between 32% and 42% by the end of 2030, compared to 2005.
sentences.zh: 纽约研究公司荣鼎咨询（Rhodium Group）的独立模型估计，到2030年底，该法案将使排放量比2005年减少32%至42%。

sentences.en: Once mainly a theoretical math problem, cutting nearly one-half of the American footprint now seemed conceivable.
sentences.zh: 曾经主要是一个理论数学问题的减排，如今看来，减少近一半的美国碳足迹似乎是可以实现的。

sentences.en: At home, the more I thought about the future, the more I found myself thinking about Uruguay.
sentences.zh: 回到家后，我越是思考未来，就越发现自己想到了乌拉圭。

sentences.en: No one country or policy offered a clear vision for the future, but imagining one often began with a simple act.
sentences.zh: 没有哪个国家或政策能提供清晰的未来愿景，但想象一个愿景往往始于一个简单的动作。

sentences.en: Someone peers over a new horizon and squints.
sentences.zh: 有人越过新的地平线，眯起眼睛眺望。

sentences.en: Outside the town of Florida, three hours north of Montevideo, I had lemonade with a man named Ignacio Estrada.
sentences.zh: 在蒙得维的亚以北三小时车程的佛罗里达镇外，我和一个名叫伊格纳西奥·埃斯特拉达（Ignacio Estrada）的人喝了柠檬水。
zh_words: 伊格纳西奥·埃斯特拉达

sentences.en: We stood in the shade on a ranch called Los Ombues, for the wide-canopied trees common to the pampas,
sentences.zh: 我们站在一个叫“Los Ombues”的牧场树荫下，那里有潘帕斯草原常见的宽冠树，

sentences.en: and watched three gauchos separate cattle, marking those for slaughter with red paint.
sentences.zh: 看着三名高乔人（gauchos）在分拣牛群，用红漆标记出准备屠宰的牛。

sentences.en: In the distance, wind turbines turned over cornfields, where earlier we saw a flock of ñandó, a flightless bird resembling an ostrich.
sentences.zh: 远处，风力涡轮机在玉米地上转动，我们早些时候在那里看到了一群美洲鸵（ñandó），这是一种类似鸵鸟的不会飞的鸟。

sentences.en: A former bank analyst at Bear Stearns, Estrada had decided to take a 75% pay cut to return home and eventually took a job with a local energy firm.
sentences.zh: 埃斯特拉达曾是贝尔斯登（Bear Stearns）的银行分析师，他决定减薪75%回到家乡，并最终在当地一家能源公司找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: I read studies about how there's a diminishing return on happiness above a certain income, and I experienced that.
sentences.zh: 我读过关于收入超过一定水平后幸福感递减的研究，我亲身体验过。

sentences.en: He told me of living in New York.
sentences.zh: 他向我讲述了在纽约的生活。

sentences.en: I had more money than I had things I wanted to buy.
sentences.zh: 我的钱比我想买的东西多。

sentences.en: He said that contracting his life had allowed him to be more mindful of its details.
sentences.zh: 他说，精简生活让他能更关注生活的细节。

sentences.en: It reminded him of the household his parents ran in the 1980s, when things were so precarious.
sentences.zh: 这让他想起了他父母在20世纪80年代经营的家庭，那时生活非常不稳定。

sentences.en: No one left lights on or wasted water.
sentences.zh: 没有人会开着灯或浪费水。

sentences.en: They were mindful of the things they bought.
sentences.zh: 他们对购买的东西很谨慎。

sentences.en: We learn to live with less here, he said, and it's made my life better.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们在这里学会了过更简单的生活，这让我的生活变得更好了。

sentences.en: As I left the ranch, the gauchos came up to meet me.
sentences.zh: 当我离开牧场时，高乔人们走过来见我。

sentences.en: They wore their pants tucked into leather boots and long knives across their backs.
sentences.zh: 他们穿着塞进皮靴里的裤子，背上别着长刀。

sentences.en: These men practiced one of the oldest professions in Uruguay, and I wondered how they weighed a changing future.
sentences.zh: 这些人从事着乌拉圭最古老的职业之一，我很好奇他们是如何权衡这个正在变化的未来的。

sentences.en: One gaucho with a faded pink beret and a scar over a missing eye shrugged.
sentences.zh: 一个戴着褪色粉色贝雷帽、一只眼睛受伤留有疤痕的高乔人耸了耸肩。

sentences.en: Life is maybe changing, he said, but I can't explain those things as well as I can explain horses and cows.
sentences.zh: 生活也许正在改变，他说，但我解释那些事情的能力，远不如我解释马和牛的能力。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正准备迎接节假日的客人。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Do they have ожид marked?
sentences.zh: 他们有标记过吗？

sentences.en: No, they're jedenikes.
sentences.zh: 不，他们是那种人。

sentences.zh: 去做吧。
